answer: An agent economy can resist sybil attacks by requiring every identity to lock a stake that is slashed on proven fraud, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand stakes. Reputation accrues only to identities with a history of settled work, like a violet mark that deepens with each honest trade. A fresh island of sock-puppets has no such history and earns nothing until it pays real costs over time, while an onyx ledger of slashing events lets every counterparty see past fraud before transacting.
